PullRequest.Title: chat: keep connector connection alive across auth session changes
PullRequest.Body:

## Problem

After connecting a Copilot connector (e.g. Work IQ) from the Chat Customizations **Browse** page and finishing the browser authorization, the card's button can keep showing **Connect**. Clicking it again makes it update, because that click runs a fresh catalog check that sees the connector is already connected.

## Cause

`CopilotConnectorsService` resets its catalog context whenever a relevant GitHub authentication session changes. That reset cancels every operation tied to the context, including the loop in `connect()` that waits for the connector to become `connected`. The first connect itself triggers such a change because `authorize()` creates a connector-scoped session (and token refreshes can do the same). So `connect()` is cancelled while the user is still in the browser, the Browse page treats it as cancelled, and nothing checks the status again.

## Fix

If a catalog reset interrupts `connect()`, it now resumes with a fresh operation instead of failing. It only does this when:

- the caller didn't cancel,
- the default account is unchanged,
- connectors are still enabled and the service isn't disposed,
- and fewer than 3 resets have happened.

The polling state (initial status, deadline, whether `pending` was observed) is preserved. So if the consent page was already opened, the connection isn't requested again, the page isn't reopened, and the original 5-minute timeout still applies. Account switches still cancel, as before.

The request and polling steps are split out of `connect()` into `requestConnection` and `pollConnection` to make the retry straightforward.

## Tests

New tests in `copilotConnectorsService.test.ts`:

- A same-account session change **before consent** doesn't abandon the connection.
- A same-account session change **while polling** doesn't abandon the connection.
- An account switch while polling still cancels the connection.

The first two failed before the fix.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/copilotConnectorsService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceInstallService.test.ts`: passed (150 tests)
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed

Not tested yet: the live Work IQ authorization flow end to end.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect or reconnect one connector from Browse/install or the embedded connector detail without an authentication-session reset
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authorization/session resolution must complete, then a catalog GET, connection PUT, optional external consent-page open, and serial catalog polling must complete before the action resolves. A connected-membership change can also await Agent Host session reconciliation inside refresh, so that IPC is on the critical path when supported.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication sessions and, only if needed, create an authorized connector session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one session lookup per connect attempt; session creation is only performed when no suitable connector-scoped session exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same authorization step preceded connect before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authorization must finish before catalog or mutation requests begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial GET plus one serial GET approximately every 2 seconds until completion, bounded by the original five-minute deadline (the existing timeout test establishes about 150 polling GETs).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial and polling catalog requests occurred at the same cadence and deadline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial GET determines whether mutation is needed; each polling GET gates detection of completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One PUT in the normal path for one connector action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single PUT occurred in connect.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must return before consent handling and polling state are established.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the external HTTPS consent page
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once in the normal path when the response supplies a valid consent link.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same consent page was opened and awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The open result is awaited before polling starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh live Agent Host connector sessions after connected membership changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for each authoritative refresh that changes connected membership; absent when the host extension is unavailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh path and reconciliation existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by refresh, so it delays the connect result when membership changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One explicitly selected connector; polling scales with authorization duration up to the fixed five-minute deadline, not catalog size beyond parsing the bounded catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations within one connect are serialized. Existing callers can initiate independent connector actions, but the diff adds no collection fan-out or new parallel scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog GETs can revalidate through the GitHub client cache/ETag. The ordinary path reuses the current client; no new cache invalidation occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the unchanged boundary calls, two-second cadence, five-minute deadline, and serial awaits are explicit in the service and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual catalog and Agent Host round-trip durations vary, but the diff leaves their normal-path cardinality and placement unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the refactor preserves normal-path network, IPC, polling, and cache behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: A same-account authentication-session change resets the catalog before the connection request has completed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The reset cancels the current catalog-bound operation. The changed loop reauthorizes, creates a fresh operation, and resumes; completion therefore waits for the replacement session lookup/client acquisition and catalog request before proceeding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve authentication sessions on each resumed attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional lookup per observed reset, capped at three resumed resets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first catalog reset canceled connect, so no replacement lookup occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each lookup must complete before a replacement catalog operation starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refetch the full connector catalog using a newly acquired account client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One replacement GET per reset before poll state exists, capped at three; the added test establishes two GETs for one pre-consent reset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reset canceled connect after the interrupted GET and did not continue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The replacement GET is required to determine whether the connector became connected and whether PUT is still needed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one PUT after the replacement GET. If reset lands after dispatch but before the PUT result is committed to pollState, an uncertain mutation can be repeated, bounded to four total attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An in-flight PUT interrupted by catalog reset was not retried by the service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A replacement or repeated PUT must complete before polling begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the consent page returned by a completed PUT
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally once. In the narrow uncertain-PUT reset race it could repeat with the repeated request, bounded by the reset cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reset canceled the action rather than reopening consent.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of relevant same-account session changes during one explicit connect; retries are capped at three and remain tied to one connector.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replacement attempts are strictly serial because each loop iteration disposes its operation before the next begins. No burst is introduced within one connect.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: resetCatalogContext clears the API client and catalog state, so each resumed attempt is cold and cannot reuse the prior ETag/client cache. The reset count bounds these cold misses; there is no negative cache involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for one added cold lookup/GET per reset and serial bounded resumption; medium for duplicate completed PUT/consent work because dispatch completion relative to cancellation is inherently uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A reset during the initial catalog GET is demonstrated by tests. A reset precisely during the PUT is possible from the same cancellation wiring but its prevalence and server-side completion are uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the added work is bounded to three resets, is necessary to preserve progress after a real session change, and has no collection or lifetime scaling. The narrow uncertain-mutation race does not provide enough evidence of a significant performance outcome to justify a performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: A same-account authentication-session change resets the catalog while consent polling is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The canceled polling GET unwinds to the changed retry loop. Reauthorization and a fresh operation/client must complete, after which polling resumes with the existing state and original deadline; no new connection request or consent open is performed once pollState exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve the active account's authentication sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One added lookup per reset, capped at three.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Polling ended with cancellation, so no resumed lookup occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before resumed polling can issue its next request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume catalog polling with GET requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One immediate replacement polling GET per reset, then the existing serial two-second cadence until the preserved deadline; at most three reset resumptions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The reset canceled the polling action and no further GET was made by that connect call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first authoritative connected/error state determines when the action completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh Agent Host sessions if resumed polling observes changed connected membership
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Membership-based, normally once when connected state is first authoritatively observed; a reset overlapping reconciliation may cause another bounded reconciliation on the next authoritative refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed, but the diff allows the action to reach it after a reset instead of terminating.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited inside refresh when membership changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session-reset count during one connector's remaining authorization window; the deadline is preserved and resets are capped at three.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Polling and reset recovery are serial. A reset cancels the old operation before the next iteration creates a replacement; no overlapping GET burst is scheduled by the changed loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each reset clears the client/catalog cache, so resumed polling starts cold; subsequent GETs on that client can revalidate. pollState retains initial status, pending observation, and deadline, preventing a second PUT and preventing timeout extension.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed pollState lifetime and reset cap prove the bounded serial behavior, and the added test proves the one-reset request sequence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of reacquiring a client and authentication sessions varies, but cardinality and the absence of deadline extension are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: additional boundary work is bounded and directly implements successful continuation, while preserving the original overall polling window and avoiding repeated mutation after pollState is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: The caller cancels, connectors are disabled/disposed, or the default account changes during connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancellation or identity/lifecycle checks terminate the action rather than entering another retry iteration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Abort any active catalog GET or connection PUT through the operation token/AbortSignal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the currently active request per connect action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These conditions canceled the active operation before the diff as well.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Abortion causes immediate rejection; no resumed request is issued when caller cancellation, lifecycle shutdown, or account mismatch is detected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user action and one active request; no dependence on connector collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No replacement operation is created after these terminal conditions. Existing independent connector actions remain independently cancellable.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Account or enablement changes reset and clear catalog state as before; the changed catch explicitly refuses reuse/retry across account identity or disabled/disposed lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every terminal condition is checked in the added catch, and account-switch behavior is covered by the added test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the performance verdict.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: terminal cancellation does not retain polling, issue replacement boundary calls, or extend resource lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced connect callers, catalog-reset ownership, authentication/session lookup, GitHub client caching, network mutation and polling, Agent Host reconciliation, cancellation, tests, and concurrency. The PR adds bounded serial recovery work after same-account catalog resets, preserves the original five-minute deadline and polling state, and does not introduce a high-confidence actionable performance regression. No finding or regression-fix learning record was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
